People still think of pharmacies as chemists.

But inside many of them, something very different is happening.

They are quietly becoming clinical diagnostic hubs.

Pharmacists are not just dispensing anymore.
They are running consultations.
Triaging conditions.
Delivering treatment.

Sounds like progress.

But here is the problem.

Most clinical services are still held together with five or six disconnected tools.

- Booking platforms that do not talk to consultation software
- Paper SOPs and policies
- WhatsApp for governance
- Spreadsheets for reporting

Too many systems.
Too much typing.
Nothing actually connected.

And this is the part nobody talks about.

The shift to clinical pharmacy is not the hard part.

Scaling it is.

What determines whether clinical pharmacy scales is not just demand, training or ambition.

It is the infrastructure behind it.

That is what Titanverse is built for.

Connecting the moving parts of clinical services so pharmacists can practise at the top of their licence, not buried in admin.

The prescribers are coming.

The infrastructure isn't.

September 2026 is five months away.

Every newly qualified pharmacist joins the register as an independent prescriber.

The NHS has already proved the model works.

33,000+ consultations across 164 pathfinder sites.
59% led to prescribing interventions that would have gone to a GP or hospital.
97% of episodes closed without onward referral.

And yet 93% of IPs in community pharmacy still can't use their qualification.

Even inside the funded NHS pilot, with dedicated IT support and ring-fenced prescribing sessions, pharmacists were dealing with multiple platforms that didn't talk to each other, duplicate data entry, and clinical governance held together by workarounds.

If it was that hard in the pilot, imagine the rest of community pharmacy.

✨ Is your pharmacy building for prescribing, or just hoping it lands cleanly?

Sources: NHS England IP Pathfinder Programme / University of Manchester NHS IP Pathfinder Evaluation, January 2026 / NHS Community Pharmacy Workforce Survey, July 2025

Independent pharmacy is not standing still.

And neither is Tas Bhatti.

As a founding member of IPCN, Tas has been close to the conversations that matter to independent contractors. The daily pressures. The big decisions. The constant question of how pharmacies keep moving forward when dispensing alone is no longer enough.

So it was brilliant to catch up with him at TitanUp 26.

There was plenty to get stuck into on the day.

✅ Robots and automation
✅ The future of PMRs
✅ Titanverse
✅ How pharmacy businesses are changing
✅ And, of course, the food did not go unnoticed ✨

But one of the best parts was hearing Tas talk about where he thinks pharmacy businesses are heading.

From dispensing pressure to the systems, services, and decisions that shape the whole pharmacy business.

A perspective worth hearing.
3 minutes with the robot. Then @Josh sums the whole thing up in two words at the end 😂

Why should a patient choose you when…

“Pharmacy is becoming Nando’s. Everyone has the same menu.”

That was @Rahul Puri’s point at TitanUp 26.

Weight management, travel, blood pressure, vaccinations, prescribing. 

More pharmacies now offer versions of the same list. The services still matter, but they are no longer enough to set you apart.

What sets you apart is what happens after the patient chooses you.

Two pharmacies can offer the same service and build completely different businesses around it. One treats the appointment as a transaction. The other turns it into a relationship.

That relationship is hard to build when the journey is held together manually.

✅ Bookings need to be simple to manage.
✅ Consultations need to be structured.
✅ Notes need to land in the right place.
✅ Follow-ups cannot rely on memory.
✅ Service history needs to be easy to see.
✅ The next step needs to be clear for the patient and the team.
✅ The whole journey needs to connect smoothly back into the PMR.

That is exactly what Titanverse is built for.

Not another item on the menu, but the system built to help pharmacies run the journey around it.

Or, as Rahul put it:

“The service is not your advantage anymore. The journey is.”

Trying to grow private services when every booking, note, payment and letter creates another job? Well… you’re not imagining it.

Bookings in one place.
Consultations in another.
Notes somewhere else.
Payments bolted on.
Letters still to write.
And no simple way to push the prescription back into your PMR.

That is where services start to feel heavier than they should.

Here’s the thing.

Everything you can see here already runs inside Titanverse.

Not bolted together.
Not coming soon.
Already live.

As @Wahid Muhammad put it at TitanUp 26:

“It’s packed, and it’s doing it already.”

✅ Payments.
✅ Bookings.

✅ Consultations.
✅ Voice transcription.

✅ Vitals.
✅ Treatment plans.
✅ Notes.

And more.

All inside one connected platform.

Because a service that holds together end to end has a much better chance of paying its way.

One that leaks at every handover stays harder to run, harder to scale and easier to leave as a side project.

That is the difference between offering private services and actually being able to build a business around them.
